correctness.rationale: Differentiate the exact normalized formula: 4(T_s^4)'=B+s(Q-P), B=3T_int^4. When high-rate P nonzero, P/(B/s+Q) strictly decreases, as every numerator decay exponent exceeds sqrt(3) while each denominator exponent is smaller or 0. This yields the sharp unique-root criterion and positive derivative outside. On P>Q, f=P-Q has negative derivative, giving monotone minimum depth and linear onset. Transverse P=Q gives finite saturation with order 1/s; if Q=0, least high exponent gives logarithmic depth. Direct exponential substitution yields the exact crossover equation. Independent numerical bisection at s=1 and 1000 reproduced depth ~0.848000916459 and ~1.352576932764 for P=60e^(-3tau), Q=4e^(-tau).
